title: AI Engineering Laboratory
intro: Practical AI work: structuring agents so they are useful in real engineering, running models locally to understand their limits, and wiring AI into workflows where it saves time. Everything here is described as it actually runs. Models are used or evaluated, not built or trained by me.

workflows.title: Multi-agent software development
workflows.description: A coordinator plans and delegates; specialist agents for frontend, backend, IoT, DevOps and security review work on feature branches and pull requests. Role definitions live in written agent instructions (AGENTS.md style).
guardrails: No merge to main, production deploy, data deletion or device change without explicit human approval on the task.
Security review is a separate role with its own escalation path.
Every task records changes, verification evidence and the next owner.

workflows.title: Persistent agent memory and project context
workflows.description: Decisions, conventions and environment facts carry between sessions so agents do not start from zero, while task-specific detail stays with the task.

workflows.title: Local LLM experiments
workflows.description: Running open models locally through Ollama to compare reasoning, tool calling and speed on consumer hardware, and to judge where local inference is good enough.

workflows.title: Model selection and fallback
workflows.description: Choosing a provider and model per task, with fallbacks when a model is unavailable or unsuitable.

workflows.title: Automation pipelines
workflows.description: n8n and scripted workflows for automated information collection, scheduled operational and market monitoring, and documentation generation.

disclaimer: Prototype agents are not presented as autonomous production systems. Human approval gates apply to every sensitive action.
